citations.quote: XOSPATA is indicated for the treatment of adult patients who have relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with a FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3) mutation as detected by an FDA-approved test.

target_moa.text: Gilteritinib is a kinase inhibitor that inhibits FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3), decreasing FLT3 receptor signaling (phosphorylation of STAT5, AKT, and ERK); it also inhibits AXL, LTK, ALK, and KIT.

citations.quote: Mechanism of ActionGilteritinib inhibits FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3) with IC50 of 0.291nM. It also has inhibitory effects on LTK, AXL, ALK, and KIT kinase activities. It showed similar activities inhibiting the growth of Ba/F3 cells expressing FLT3-ITD, FLT3-D835Y or FLT3-ITD-D835Y.

In studies to elucidate its mechanism of action, gilteritinib demonstrated the ability to inhibit FLT3 receptor signaling, e.g., decreasing phosphorylation of signal transducer and activator of transcription 5 (STAT5), protein kinase B (AKT), and extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK).
Gilteritinib (ASP2215) is an orally-available small molecule drug to treat adult patients with R/R AML with an FLT3 mutation.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) were myalgia/arthralgia, transaminase increase, fatigue/malaise, fever, noninfectious diarrhea, dyspnea, edema, rash, pneumonia, nausea, stomatitis, cough, headache, hypotension, dizziness and vomiting. Potentially life-threatening/serious risks included QT prolongation (1.4% had QTcF >500 msec), differentiation syndrome, and pancreatitis.
